payload.claim: The spec declares no `risk` field in its frontmatter (so `declared_risk` is `None`, defaulting to `"standard"`), even though its own `touches` list includes `saffron/cell/session.py`, which matches this repo's `.saffron/policy.yaml` `elevate_on: saffron/cell/**` pattern. Every spec sampled in `.saffron/specs/done/` that touches `saffron/cell/session.py` explicitly declares `risk: elevated`. The runtime still computes `effective_risk` fresh from the real diff at gate time regardless of the declaration (`saffron/repos/policy.py::effective_risk`, and DESIGN.md's "The tier is computed afresh from it (§5.6)"), so the cell's actual gates (`size` becoming blocking, etc.) will behave correctly with or without the field, and the measured ~438 non-test changed tokens clear the `bug` ceiling of 1300 either way — so nothing the cell builds is wrong on this account. But the task's ledger row records only the spec's own `declared_risk` at creation time, before any diff exists, which is what feeds the morning queue's risk-based sort/visibility ("so you read it cold rather than skim," per DESIGN.md's risk-tiering passage) — so unlike its siblings, this spec's task won't surface as elevated in the queue until its diff actually lands. This isn't a build or scope blocker since the cell's own output is unaffected either way, but a person should decide, before the cell starts, whether to add `risk: elevated` for consistency with the repo's own established practice for this exact touched path.
